The La0.008Al0.08FeCoCrNiMn HEA was prepared by medium-frequency induction melting in a high-purify argon environment.
the molten alloy was sucked into an yttrium oxide tube (inner diameter: 6 mm, external diameter: 8 mm) and quenched into the 25 °C liquid metal (Ga-In-Sn) rapidly.
The Φ6 mm ingot was subjected to cold rolling (CR) using a laboratory-scale rolling mill to a final thickness of ~0.7 mm, reducing 88.3%.

The matrix of the HEA is the FCC phase.
The σ phase was precipitated during the annealing process, mainly, after annealing at 600 ◦C for 64 min, the diffraction peaks of the σ phase became more and more obviously
The diameters of the precipitated particles were mainly distributed between 5 and 30 nm, and the mean size was 20.2 nm.
Grain morphologies in Fig. 3 (a) were deformed elongate grains due to the severe cold rolling.
The deformed elongated grains and the recrystallized grains in Fig. 3 (b) exhibit the typical partial recrystallization grain structures after annealing at 600 ◦C for 32 min.
Most grains have recrystallized when annealing at 600 ◦C for 128 min, as shown in Fig. 3 (c).
Almost all the grains have recrystallized after annealing at 600 ◦C for 360 min, as exhibited in Fig. 3 (d).

a large number of nano-twins and nano-sized grains were observed under annealing at 600 ◦C for 1 min, as shown in Fig. 5 (a). The nano-twins passed through the grains, and the thickness of such nano-twins was about 10 nm.
